thread:
Zoe (Support): heads up — AcmeCorp just escalated. They say outputs got way more 'creative' after this morning's rollout (09:03 UTC). Previously templated replies were deterministic; now same prompt returns very different phrasings and a couple hallucinations. They attached examples.
Zoe (Support): example from customer: 
> prompt: "Summarize this policy in one sentence."
> old response (last week): "Policy A restricts external file sharing without approval."
> new responses (today): "It limits who can send files out, basically a permissions gate." / "A security rule that blocks outside sharing by default unless approved." + one reply saying "Check internal policy doc 17B" (hallucinated).
Zoe (Support): they noticed the delta right after our 09:03 deploy id `deploy-2026-02-12-0903` (they timestamped the first changed response at 09:11 UTC).
Miguel (Infra): pinging runtime /deploy logs — which deploy exactly? I see `deploy-2026-02-12-0903` rolled config changes & a tiny runtime tweak. Deploybot?

deploy-bot: deployed `deploy-2026-02-12-0903` by @samir, services: model-router, config-service, model-runtime. rollout: 09:03-09:07 UTC.

Samir (Runtime): I pushed a config default change earlier to address a latency/cost regression. It was intended to only affect a canary pool but I might have accidentally promoted the sampling profile to the default. Checking PR notes...

Samir (Runtime): PR #987: "default sampling profile: enable mild sampling to reduce under-generation on long contexts" — I see the ops flag got flipped during merge and then propagated. Oops.

Samir (Runtime): here's the config diff that probably caused it:
```
# configs/model_defaults.yaml (before)
sampling:
  temperature: 0.0  # deterministic default used in prod for few-shot templates
  top_p: 1.0

# configs/model_defaults.yaml (after deploy-2026-02-12-0903)
sampling:
  temperature: 0.6
  top_p: 0.92
```

Zoe (Support): that matches customer observations (more variability). They are already on a Dedicated instance but rely on our default sampling when they don't set override params.

Priya (SRE): severity? customer is on Dedicated with Performance SLA. If outputs degrade we have to treat as P1. Are they threatening to rollback to previous version of their app?

Zoe (Support): they're upset, asked for immediate mitigation. Customer impact: 3 production flows affected, one workflow with legal text produced a hallucination. They're asking for rollback or toggle to previous deterministic defaults.

Miguel (Infra): can we hotflip default profile back to previous values? If config-service supports dynamic flags we can patch without a full redeploy. Checking whether this config is served from the centralized config-service or baked into images.

Samir (Runtime): it is served via config-service but we accidentally promoted the profile to the global default key `models.default.sampling`. I can push a rollback change to set that key back to the safe values. I'll prepare a hotfix and test on canary.

Samir (Runtime): repro steps for us to validate locally (soops customer repro):
1) curl to our hosted inference endpoint using a request that omits sampling params (so we rely on server defaults)
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.inference/v1/generate \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"gpt-3k-prod","input":"Summarize this policy in one sentence."}'
```
2) Observe different outputs across repeated calls (~0.6 temp behaviour).
3) After config patching to temperature:0.0 top_p:1.0 the same curl should return the old deterministic reply.

Priya (SRE): test plan — Samir, push a config-service patch to revert `models.default.sampling` to previous values, route to 10% canary, run 50 repeated requests to compare variance. If passes, promote to 100%. I'll stand by to watch for any perf regressions.

Samir (Runtime): doing that now. Hotfix branch: `hotfix/restore-deterministic-defaults`. Patch: 
```yaml
# patch applied to config-service via k8s configmap update
models:
  default:
    sampling:
      temperature: 0.0
      top_p: 1.0
```

Miguel (Infra): FYI we should also add an explicit test in the deploy pipeline that checks whether default sampling changed relative to the previous release to avoid accidental promotion.

Zoe (Support): I told AcmeCorp we'll have a fix in ~45m and will update them when rollback completes. They asked for the commit/PR so they can track the change; I gave them PR #987 and told them we're rolling back.

Samir (Runtime): canary patch applied at 09:28 UTC. Running synthetic checks...

Priya (SRE): can you paste quick variance numbers from the canary run? 50 requests before vs after.

Samir (Runtime): before (with temperature 0.6): entropy of response set was high, saw ~22 unique phrasings out of 50. after (reverted): 1 canonical phrasing + 2 minor punctuation variants.

Samir (Runtime): promoting to 100% now.

deploy-bot: rolled `hotfix/restore-deterministic-defaults` to config-service and model-router; rollout completed 09:42 UTC.

Zoe (Support): customer update sent at 09:45 UTC — they confirm behavior looks back to normal, no hallucinations in their quick smoke. They want formal postmortem and an assurance this won't be silently promoted again.

Miguel (Infra): follow-ups — add a pre-merge CI guard that fails if global defaults change without an explicit changelog entry + ops approval. Also make the default sampling key require an explicit opt-in to be non-zero.

Priya (SRE): logging action — create incident ticket, attach deploy timeline, include canary logs and variance numbers. Samir, please attach the PR and config diffs. Zoe, keep the customer slack thread open and offer a follow-up call.

Zoe (Support): will do. Thanks team. :heart:

Priya (SRE): tagging postmortem owner @samir to lead, due EOD.

Samir (Runtime): acknowledged, will write up root cause and the mitigation steps (hotfix, CI guard, docs).
